sources.cite: AWS Certified Advanced Networking - Specialty (ANS-C01) exam guide: Network Design 30%, Network Implementation 26%, Network Management and Operation 20%, Network Security, Compliance, and Governance 24%

sources.cite: Elastic Load Balancing User Guide: Health checks for Application Load Balancer target groups
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-16 (no last-updated date shown). Relevant text: interval 'The default is 30 seconds' for instance targets; timeout 5 seconds; HealthyThresholdCount 'The default is 5'; UnhealthyThresholdCount 'The default is 2'; Matcher 'The default value is 200'; reason code Target.ResponseCodeMismatch, 'Health checks failed with these codes: [code]'; 'If a target group contains only unhealthy registered targets, the load balancer routes requests to all those targets, regardless of their health status ... the load balancer fails open.'

sources.cite: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling User Guide: Health checks for instances in an Auto Scaling group
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-16. Relevant text: 'When Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling determines that an InService instance is unhealthy, it replaces it with a new instance to maintain the desired capacity of the group'; Elastic Load Balancing is one of the sources that can report an instance unhealthy; the checks begin after a health check grace period. The default grace period was not stated on the page, so the scenario gives the group's setting.
